name: Tetragametic Chimerism Syndrome

criteria.description: Identification of two or more genetically distinct cell lines derived from different zygotes in one individual
Presence of discordant physical or phenotypic features suggestive of chimerism (e.g., patchy skin pigmentation, asymmetrical organ development)
Exclusion of other causes of mosaicism such as postzygotic mutation or somatic mosaicism

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Genetic confirmation of two or more distinct cell lines plus phenotypic evidence of chimerism
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires specialized genetic testing such as STR analysis or SNP microarray

searchTerms: areas of skin with less color

pathognomonic.symptomName: Gonadal dysgenesis with female appearance, male
searchTerms: gonadal development failure with female appearance in males
sex development disorder with female traits

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abnormality of multiple cell lineages in the bone marrow
searchTerms: multiple blood cell types abnormal in marrow
bone marrow affecting several cell lines

laboratory: Detection of two or more distinct DNA profiles in blood or tissue samples via STR or SNP analysis
Discordant blood group antigens in different tissues
Karyotype showing presence of multiple cell lines
imaging: Asymmetrical organ size or development on ultrasound, MRI, or CT
Renal hypoplasia or other structural anomalies
genetic: Presence of two or more genetically distinct cell populations originating from different zygotes
No evidence of postzygotic mutation mosaicism
other: Patchy skin pigmentation along Blaschko lines
Discordant phenotypic sex characteristics in some cases

distinguishingFeatures: Mosaicism arises from a single zygote with postzygotic mutation
Genetic differences limited to somatic mutations, not distinct zygotes
Genetic differences confined to placenta, not present in multiple tissues

redFlags: Discordant blood group or sex chromosome karyotypes in different tissues
Patchy or segmental skin pigmentation abnormalities
Presence of two genetically distinct cell populations confirmed by DNA analysis
references: Strain L, et al. Tetragametic chimerism: clinical and genetic features. Am J Med Genet A. 2019.
Biesecker LG. Mosaicism and chimerism in human disease. Nat Rev Genet. 2013.
